semantic_differences: Capability binds the target-language editor visit object (a one-to-one representation of the mounted outlet identity under passive rendering); native references/pointers or actual framework-owned object identity are used, never document-key equality.

Native queue receipts use copied immutable string values and durable value records. JSON is a trusted resource/observation boundary; no cross-runtime mutable-object or JS Object.freeze identity equivalence is claimed.
All integration and native callbacks are synchronous and may reenter command dispatch; no Promise acknowledgement, thread race or mandatory deferral substitutes for them.

The native embedding serializes passive observations as JSON values; native repository listener snapshots and closures execute synchronously in the native process. No cross-runtime mutable event-reference equivalence is asserted.
Framework reactive render updates use the real framework flush, while store writes and command return are synchronous. Tests inspect passive output at write and actual DOM after the framework flush.
